keyFindings.finding: Total consolidated backlog reached $176.0 billion as of June 30, 2026, expanding by $13.0 billion sequentially. Long-term Contractual Service Agreements (CSAs) and long-cycle equipment commitments represent over $115 billion of total backlog.
keyFindings.implication: Multi-year revenue visibility anchored by high-margin aftermarket recurring cash flows

keyFindings.finding: Power segment gas turbine equipment backlog and slot reservation agreements expanded to 116 GW, with production slots effectively committed through 2029.
keyFindings.implication: Substantial pricing power and working capital inflows from non-refundable slot reservation fees

keyFindings.finding: Electrification segment orders rose 66% organically to $6.3 billion, with AI data center orders exceeding $5.0 billion in H1 2026.
keyFindings.implication: Accelerating revenue conversion in high-margin grid solutions and substations

sections.section: MD&A - Contractual Service Agreements (CSAs) Duration & Durability

keyFindings.finding: GE Vernova's CSA portfolio covers over 2,200 heavy-duty gas turbines globally. CSAs typically span 10 to 25 years in initial duration, containing contractual price-escalation formulas tied to regional inflation and actual fired operating hours.
keyFindings.implication: Defensive inflation pass-through mechanism and counter-cyclical recurring service gross margins exceeding 35%

keyFindings.finding: Historical renewal rates across gas turbine CSAs exceed 95%, reflecting prohibitive operational switching risks and non-OEM warranty disincentives for grid operators.
keyFindings.implication: Exceptional switching costs sustaining GEV's wide economic moat

sections.section: Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements - Contingencies & Warranties

keyFindings.finding: The Wind segment recognized $320 million in incremental warranty reserves and estimated contract loss provisions during Q2 2026, primarily related to Haliade-X offshore turbine blade remediation and contractual disputes.
keyFindings.implication: Continued GAAP operating margin compression within Wind until legacy offshore backlog is burned off

keyFindings.finding: On April 2026, a Massachusetts federal court granted a preliminary injunction preventing GE Vernova from terminating its supply and maintenance contract with Vineyard Wind, compelling continued fulfillment while arbitration proceeds.
keyFindings.implication: Legal and operational overhang persists on offshore commitments, though financial exposure remains ring-fenced
